note: Phase 8 (Decompiler Quality) is executed by one owner on one living integration branch, so there is a single lane. The manifest exists because ownership is what makes 'may this change touch that file' a checkable property (EP-002, EP-004), and because contract, generated and forbidden paths must be explicit even when nobody can race for them. Phase 8 edits the shared decompiler, which is protected userscript runtime, so the same lane is also the generated-output and release owner (EP-003, EP-008, EP-009).

forbiddenRationale.js/semantics/**: Semantic IR, CFG, SSA, MemorySSA and the effect model are Phase 3/6 truth. Phase 8 consumes them through their published seams. A decompiler optimization that needs to edit them is creating a second semantic engine (Master Architecture §2, P8-INV-002).
forbiddenRationale.js/analysis/**: Alias, points-to, escape, summary, type-constraint and debug facts are Phase 7 truth. A missing upstream fact is repaired at its owner layer, never faked by a private decompiler heuristic (P8-INV-003).
forbiddenRationale.js/targets/**: Architecture and ABI decoding stay behind the target boundary. A generic optimizer change that needs a decoder edit is leaking architecture semantics into the middle end (P8-INV-004).
forbiddenRationale.js/core/identity/**: Artifact and instruction identity is a Phase 0/4 contract; Phase 8 keys artifacts with it rather than redefining it.
forbiddenRationale.js/core/artifacts/**: ArtifactStore invalidation semantics are a Phase 4 contract. Phase 8 declares new artifact kinds through the existing descriptor contract.
forbiddenRationale.js/platform/capability-maturity.js: Phase 8 reads capability truth to build its corpus manifest. Promoting maturity is a separate, evidence-backed change.
forbiddenRationale.docs/HEX_MASTER_ARCHITECTURE.md: A phase may not edit the contract it is being judged against.
forbiddenRationale.tests/phase7/**: Earlier-phase evidence may be re-run and its helpers imported read-only, but Phase 8 must not rewrite it.

ownedWithConstraint.js/decompiler/pipeline-core.js: The production decompiler entry point. Phase 8 may register passes and publish Phase 8 results here. It must not begin reading instruction mnemonic/operand text or decoder internals; that boundary stays enforced by MIGRATION_GUARDRAILS and tests/migration-guardrails.mjs.
ownedWithConstraint.package.json: May add Phase 8 scripts and wire them into existing aggregates. Must not remove or weaken an existing gate.
ownedWithConstraint.userscript/hex.user.template.js: Generated output. It MUST be produced by the canonical builder (npm run userscript:build) and committed by the integration owner after each accepted checkpoint. It must never be hand-edited or copied from another branch.
ownedWithConstraint.userscript/release-version.json: Generated release identity. It advances deterministically from protected runtime content and must never be edited by hand.
ownedWithConstraint.docs/PHASE8_CHECKPOINT.md: The living checkpoint record. It records what was accepted with which evidence; it may not relax an exit gate.
ownedWithConstraint.docs/PHASE8_HANDOFF.md: The handoff record: current state, open work and the traps that cost time. It may not relax an exit gate.

generatedOutputNote: Phase 8 edits js/decompiler/**, which is part of the protected userscript runtime, so the canonical userscript build output changes with every accepted checkpoint. Phase 8 is a single-owner phase and is therefore also the release owner: it MUST complete the generated-output transaction itself (rebuild with the canonical builder, commit, rebuild again and require a zero diff) before accepting the next dependent checkpoint. Changing protected runtime source without rebuilding is a merge-blocking desync (EP-003, EP-008, EP-009). js/userscript/deployment-identity.generated.js is deliberately not owned here: it records the commit a deployment was built from, is written by the Workers build, and differs between a local build and a CI checkout by design.
